name: Aitape
reason: Rule 2/1: Wikivoyage Sepik names it only as a mission town and a pointer to Sissano Lagoon; no See/Do listing, nothing a visitor does for half an hour.
objection: Harbour towns on a coastal route can be second-tier stops, and it sits on the Wewak-Vanimo road; but no source gives a sight or activity there.

name: Maprik
reason: Rule 1-3: Wikivoyage Sepik and Remote Lands both name the Maprik area for the best haus tambaran spirit houses; a visitor can visit them. Kept as the one entry for the area (duplicate 'Maprik Haus Tambaran' rejected).
objection: Haus tambaran visits go through village tours and are not always open to outsiders; the pin is a town point, not a specific house.

name: Angoram
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Sepik) names it as a road-accessible river village, the lower-Sepik start of trips.
objection: For: main road gateway to the Sepik by road from Wewak, a harbour-town style stop. Against: no sight or activity listed, one source, mostly a launching point.

name: Ambunti
reason: Rule 1: PTPA Momase names it only as the festival host; Remote Lands lists it as a Sepik region hub. Upper Sepik base for crocodile and bird trips.
objection: For: recognised upper-Sepik village a guide treats as a destination. Against: the counted mention is the festival (an event), no permanent sight described.

name: Pagwi
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Sepik) lists it as a road-accessible river village near the Chambri Lakes.
objection: For: road access point for Middle Sepik canoe trips. Against: a transit village with guesthouses, no sight described.

name: Timbunke
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage Sepik lists it only among road-accessible villages; the massacre site comes from Wikipedia and is not a visitor sight.
objection: A river village with a counted mention could be a place; but nothing says what a visitor does there.

name: Telefomin
reason: Rule 1/2: re-looked; Wikivoyage Sepik names it only as one of the most remote towns, no See/Do, reached by air only.
objection: Mission museum and fossils (Wikipedia only) might be a draw; no visitor source says so.

name: Sepik River
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Sepik Do, PTPA Momase 'Cruise The Sepik River' and Remote Lands all name it as the experience; a river kept as an experience, pinned at a main access point (Angoram, with Wewak/Pagwi alternatives).
objection: A long linear feature of ~1,100 km and visits are via operators or village stops; the pin choice is arbitrary and it overlaps river-village entries.

name: Chambri Lakes
reason: Rule 1: re-looked; PTPA's Sepik Adventure Tours business listing and tour itineraries (Aibom pottery, Wombun haus tambaran) name it as a stop, but no editorial counted page found.
objection: For: genuine river-trip stop with a pottery village. Against: sourcing is operator material only; seasonal water level.

name: Murik Lakes
reason: Rule 1: re-looked, no counted source and no article.
objection: Plausible river-mouth stop with villages, but only tour material.

name: Sissano Lagoon
reason: Rule 2/3: Wikivoyage mentions it only as the 1998 tsunami site near Aitape; no visitor facilities or activity.
objection: A disaster site some visitors may pause at; a single mention, nothing to do.

name: Robuin Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Sepik and Remote Lands both name it, as an uninhabited WWII fuel-dump island off Wewak.
objection: For: two counted sources and a day-trip island like Kairiru and Mushu. Against: uninhabited, owned by Wom village, no facilities and no coordinates found; needs landowner permission.

name: Wuvulu Island
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Wikivoyage Sepik) for diving. Administratively Manus Province: belongs to the islands (Manus) region, not this one.
objection: For: Cousteau-cited diving, a real destination. Against: one source here and outside this region; route to the Manus pass.

name: Cape Wom
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Wewak and PTPA Momase name the Wom Memorial and Japanese Peace Park; surrender site with open Japanese tunnels and guns, a half-hour-plus visit.
objection: Condition of tunnels and site is uncertain, and part of it is a memorial.

name: Wom Beach
reason: Rule 3: near-duplicate of Cape Wom, ~500 m away; the same stop. Mention the beach in the Cape Wom bio.
objection: PTPA names it separately and beaches are second-tier keeps; but it is the same visit.

name: Mission Hill
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (PTPA Momase 'main attractions'), no description found.
objection: For: a lookout PTPA lists as a main Wewak attraction. Against: a single listing, no description, short visit.

name: Grand Chief Sir Michael Somare Memorial
reason: Rule 3: minor memorial, one listing, no visitor activity; pin only inferred.
objection: PTPA lists it as a main attraction and Somare is nationally important.

name: Vanimo Headlands
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Remote Lands 'The Headland'): limestone peninsula with beaches and snorkelling; overlaps the Vanimo Surf Breaks pin at Vanimo Point.
objection: For: named experience (beaches, snorkelling, villages). Against: one source, an area not a site, near-duplicate pin with Vanimo Surf Breaks.

name: Japanese Barge Wreck, Vanimo
reason: Rule 3: part of the Vanimo headlands per Remote Lands; no name or position anywhere.
objection: A wartime wreck is a real quirk; but it cannot be located.

name: Maprik Haus Tambaran
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Maprik, which is the kept entry for the haus tambaran area; no single house is sited.
objection: Two counted sources; but it is the same place as Maprik.

name: Palimbei
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Remote Lands, Palambe village haus tambaran and sago demonstration), no coordinates and spelling varies.
objection: For: a named village visit with a haus tambaran. Against: one operator-style source, no pin, only via tour.

name: Mindimbit
reason: Rule 1: one counted source (Remote Lands): Iatmul village known for carved moon-faced figures and masks, with a men's spirit house.
objection: For: a named craft village visit. Against: single source, tour access only.

name: Kanganaman
reason: Rule 2: Remote Lands mentions only a village guesthouse; lodging, not a sight.
objection: The village sits among Sepik cultural stops; the source does not describe a sight.

name: Torricelli Mountains
reason: Rule 1: re-looked, only Wikipedia; no visitor source.
objection: A real range with tree kangaroos; nothing a visitor can do.

name: Bewani Mountains
reason: Rule 1: re-looked, only Wikipedia.
objection: Biodiversity range; no visitor access described.

name: Prince Alexander Mountains
reason: Rule 1: re-looked, only Wikipedia.
objection: Abelam yam culture link; no visit described.

name: Sepik Crocodile and Arts Festival
reason: Rule 4: annual festival, an event, though two counted sources name it. Mention in Ambunti/Sepik description or best-time text.
objection: Two sources and a headline cultural draw; still an occasion.

name: Sepik Bilum and Basket Show
reason: Rule 4: annual three-day show, an event.
objection: None strong; it is a dated event.
